text:
This is Alex Ovechkin's final season, and it has not gone the way anyone in Washington hoped. The 41-year-old, who announced in September that this would be his farewell year, is goalless in 11 straight games, the second-longest drought of his career, and his ice time is down to a career-low 13:47 a night, according to TSN. Our numbers see a real cold spell: 2 points in his last ten games against 4.8 expected. Spencer Carbery has said he likes what he sees underneath.

Tom Wilson is in the same rut, with 1 point in ten against 5.5 expected. Wilson avoided a suspension for his hit on Florida's Sandis Vilmanis, and Jakob Chychrun's hit on Ottawa's Nick Cousins was reviewed on the ice, with the major penalty taken off entirely.

The Capitals themselves are fine, if unremarkable. At 10-7-0 with 20 points they have about half of the expected goals (49.8%, the quality of chances for and against) and sit about two points above what they've earned. Our numbers give them a 55% chance at the playoffs.

The forwards are where the hope is. Alex Tuch, Dylan Strome and Jordan Kyrou drive the top line, and Boone Jenner, Justin Sourdif and Ryan Leonard have taken 73% of the expected goals in limited time. The worry is discipline: the Caps take 4.24 minors a game and draw 3.47, and their power play creates only 0.53 expected goals a game.
headline: Ovechkin's farewell tour hits a cold stretch
